Kødet er mildt og moderat blånende. Sporerne måler 12,5-14 x 4,5-5 µm. Den vokser med løvtræer, gerne eg og bøg, på leret, rig jord.

attributes.bogtekst_gyldendal_en:
Butyriboletus fuscoroseus is a medium-sized, grey-rose to vinaceous-brown Butyriboletus with small, yellow pores. The stem has a yellow reticulum towards the apex and typically a reddish belt lower down. The flesh is mild and moderately bluing. The spores measure 12.5–14 × 4.5–5 µm. Occurs with deciduous trees, mostly Quercus and Fagus, on clay-rich soils in thermophilic forests.
The most similar species, B. roseogriseus, occurs predominantly with Abies in upland areas of central Europe and should completely lack red on the stem. Butyriboletus fechtneri is also very similar but has a pale grey, almost silvery, cap surface. Butyriboletus appendiculatus has a ± clay-buff cap, and the flesh does not stain blue; B. regius also has flesh that does not change colour. Caloboletus radicans looks similar, but is bitter-tasting and has strongly bluing flesh.
Southern and local, extending as far north as southern Denmark; mainly July–October.
